summary: Ronin Bridge is the bridge associated with the Ronin network. It is included because of the March 2022 validator-key compromise and large reported loss, followed by attribution, recovery, and reimbursement-related aftermath.
notes: Seed record focused on the 2022 incident and aftermath rather than live bridge safety.

summary: Wormhole is a cross-chain messaging and asset-transfer protocol. It is included because of the February 2022 exploit involving wrapped ETH on Solana and a widely reported loss of more than $300 million, followed by rapid backfilling of the bridge deficit.
notes: Seed record focused on the 2022 Wormhole exploit and bridge deficit backfill.

summary: Nomad Bridge suffered a message-verification exploit in August 2022 and later relaunched a restricted recovery-oriented bridge flow. New canonical-token deposits remained disabled while affected users could bridge back assets and access pro-rata recovered funds.
notes: Classified as limited because the official recovery bridge relaunched while unrestricted new deposits remained disabled.

summary: Harmony Horizon Bridge is included because of the June 2022 exploit commonly reported at about $100 million. The incident was later attributed by the FBI to Lazarus Group actors, and the bridge's recovery/reimbursement aftermath remains historically significant.
terminal_reason: Major exploit followed by unresolved recovery/reimbursement status in this seed record.
notes: Seed record focused on the 2022 Horizon Bridge exploit and later attribution/recovery context.

summary: Poly Network is included because of the August 2021 exploit commonly reported at more than $600 million. The case is historically important because most or all of the stolen funds were later returned, making it a distinct recovery-centered bridge incident pattern.
notes: Seed record focused on the 2021 exploit and fund-return aftermath rather than live protocol safety.

summary: BSC Token Hub was the native bridge between BNB Beacon Chain and BNB Smart Chain. It is included because of the October 2022 forged-proof exploit that created two million BNB, and because the bridge was later retired as part of BNB Chain Fusion.
terminal_reason: Cross-chain communication between BNB Beacon Chain and BNB Smart Chain was disabled during the Beacon Chain final sunset.
brand_history_notes: The historical native bridge was retired during BNB Chain Fusion; the later BNB Chain Bridge is a separate aggregation interface using external bridge partners.
notes: Seed record distinguishes the nominal value of two million BNB minted from the smaller amount reported as moved off-chain and unrecovered.

summary: Multichain was a cross-chain router and bridge protocol formerly known as Anyswap. It is included because of the July 2023 abnormal MPC-controlled asset outflows of more than $125 million and the subsequent announcement that operations would cease.
terminal_reason: Operations ceased after loss of operational access and funding, following abnormal asset movements and the detention of key personnel described by the team.
brand_history_notes: Originally operated as Anyswap before rebranding to Multichain.
notes: Seed record treats the cause as unresolved and preserves both external-compromise and insider-control interpretations as competing claims.

summary: Orbit Bridge is a multi-chain interoperability service developed by Ozys. It is included because the Ethereum vault lost approximately $81.5 million in January 2024, followed by a prolonged recovery plan and partial resumption of non-Ethereum bridge functions.
brand_history_notes: After the incident, Orbit Bridge functions and assets were progressively migrated toward the Silicon and Polygon Agglayer architecture.
notes: Seed record treats the service as limited: some bridge functions resumed, while Ethereum-vault asset recovery and normalization remained incomplete.

summary: QBridge was Qubit Finance's Ethereum-to-BNB Chain bridge and cross-chain collateral pathway. It is included because a January 2022 deposit-logic flaw allowed unbacked xETH minting and the withdrawal of roughly $80 million in assets from Qubit lending markets.
terminal_reason: QBridge functions were disabled after the exploit, and reviewed reopening announcements covered Qubit lending markets rather than the bridge itself.
brand_history_notes: QBridge was the cross-chain component of Qubit Finance; later Qubit market reopening and DAO governance announcements did not establish that the bridge resumed.
notes: Seed record distinguishes the bridge's terminal status from the partial reopening of Qubit lending markets and ongoing compensation mechanisms.

summary: THORChain is a cross-chain liquidity network and native-asset exchange protocol. It is included because two ETH Router exploits in July 2021 caused a combined protocol insolvency of about $16 million, and a separate May 2026 GG20 TSS exploit drained approximately $10.7 million from an Asgard vault. Normal trading remained temporarily paused at the latest review.
notes: The 2021 router losses were covered through treasury-led recovery and the network later reopened. The May 2026 vault loss remains under investigation and governance-led recovery review. The official site and June 11 restart update still described trading as temporarily paused at verification time.

summary: Meter Passport is Meter Network's cross-chain messaging and asset-transfer bridge. It is included because a February 2022 false-deposit vulnerability enabled unbacked BNB and WETH minting, caused approximately $4.25 million in direct losses, and led to a compensation program before the bridge was rebuilt and restored.
brand_history_notes: The exploited implementation was later replaced by audited Meter Passport versions based on newer ChainBridge contracts.
notes: Current documentation describes Meter Passport V2.0. The long-term completion of the PASS-token compensation liability remains a separate historical question.

summary: Allbridge Core is a native stablecoin bridge connecting EVM and non-EVM networks. It is included because its BNB Chain liquidity pools were exploited in April 2023 and its Solana stablecoin pools were exploited in July 2026. After the 2026 incident, Core was paused and then relaunched without liquidity pools using CCTP and LayerZero transfer routes.
brand_history_notes: Allbridge Classic is a separate deprecated product line; the active current bridge is Allbridge Core.
notes: The April 2023 incident affected the earlier BNB Chain liquidity-pool design. On July 19, 2026, Allbridge reported a second Core security incident involving a $1.65 million withdrawal from liquidity pools on Solana. Core was paused and later relaunched without liquidity pools using CCTP and LayerZero while the team accelerated its transition toward Allbridge Next. Final attacker-fund recovery and affected-LP compensation remain unverified in this reviewed batch.

summary: LI.FI is a cross-chain liquidity aggregation and orchestration protocol that routes through bridges and exchanges. It is included because approval-related smart-contract vulnerabilities caused user-wallet losses in March 2022 and July 2024, while the protocol later resumed and continued expanding.
brand_history_notes: Previously described publicly as Li Finance before adopting the LI.FI brand.
notes: The protocol remained active and reported major product and integration growth in 2026. Recovery and reimbursement claims are retained separately for each incident.

summary: ChainSwap is a permissionless cross-chain asset bridge and aggregation protocol. It is included because two separate July 2021 exploits caused approximately $800,000 and $4 million in reported losses, followed by compensation programs and an August 2021 relaunch.
brand_history_notes: The 2021 incident records used the ASAP governance-token era of ChainSwap; the current site uses the ChainSwap and CSWAP branding.
notes: The bridge relaunched after the July 2021 incidents. Final completion of every compensation obligation remains unverified in this reviewed batch.

summary: Celer cBridge is a non-custodial cross-chain asset bridge operated within the Celer Network ecosystem. It is included because an August 2022 DNS cache-poisoning incident redirected some frontend users to malicious contracts, causing approximately $240,000 in reported losses before the frontend was restored.
notes: The 2022 incident affected the frontend and DNS path rather than establishing a compromise of the underlying bridge contracts.

summary: SOCKET Protocol provides cross-chain routing and interoperability infrastructure, including the Bungee interface and Socket Gateway contracts. It is included because a January 2024 approval-related exploit caused approximately $3.3 million in reported losses, followed by rapid restoration and recovery of 1,032 ETH.
brand_history_notes: Bungee is treated as a product/interface of the SOCKET ecosystem in this batch rather than as a separate canonical bridge entity.
notes: The recovered 1,032 ETH is recorded separately from the reported $3.3 million incident amount. Final distribution completion requires later review.

summary: pNetwork operated pTokens wrapped-asset bridges and later a broader cross-chain routing protocol. It is included because the pBTC-on-BSC bridge lost 277 BTC in September 2021, the pGALA bridge required an emergency whitehat response in November 2022, and the official pTokens application now states that pNetwork v2 has reached end of life.
brand_history_notes: pNetwork v1 launched in March 2020 as the pTokens bridge. pNetwork v2 expanded the system into cross-chain routing and messaging. The official application now labels v2 end-of-life and allows redemption only with explicit risk and timing warnings.
notes: The DAO interfaces may remain available, but the bridge application itself states that pNetwork v2 has reached end of life. Final completion of the pBTC compensation process and pGALA redistribution remains unverified.

summary: Rainbow Bridge is the trustless, permissionless canonical bridge connecting Ethereum, NEAR, and Aurora. It is included because fabricated-block attacks in May and August 2022 were challenged before user funds were lost, and because official disclosures document additional critical vulnerabilities, a security pause during Ethereum's Merge, and subsequent reactivation.
brand_history_notes: Rainbow Bridge 2.0 unified earlier Ethereum-to-NEAR and Aurora bridge interfaces under rainbowbridge.app.
notes: The two canonical incidents are thwarted fabricated-block attacks. Attacker bond losses are not recorded as bridge or user losses. Privately disclosed vulnerabilities are modeled as security events rather than exploited incidents.

summary: Synapse Protocol provides cross-chain bridging, liquidity, and messaging infrastructure. It is included because a November 2021 bug in the nUSD metapool implementation allowed price manipulation and an attempted extraction of approximately $8.2 million in nUSD, but validators remained offline and did not process the malicious bridge transaction, allowing affected liquidity providers to be made whole.
brand_history_notes: Synapse was introduced as an expansion of the earlier Nerve project. This record does not merge the later, separately operated Nerve Bridge incident into Synapse.
notes: The official postmortem states that no funds were ultimately lost and that affected Avalanche nUSD liquidity providers would be made whole. Final distribution completion is not independently established in this batch.

summary: NerveNetwork is a heterogeneous-chain interoperability network whose Nerve Bridge and swap-pool infrastructure connects assets across multiple chains. It is included because a November 2021 metapool exploit drained the fUSDT and UST pool liquidity on BNB Chain and yielded approximately 900 BNB to the attacker.
brand_history_notes: The canonical entity is NerveNetwork; Nerve Bridge is treated as its bridge application. It remains separate from Synapse Protocol despite historical naming overlap and shared vulnerable metapool code lineage.
notes: No stable official postmortem or final reimbursement statement was located for the November 2021 event. Root-cause and amount claims therefore rely primarily on independent security analysis.

summary: Holograph Protocol operated as an omnichain tokenization protocol intended to preserve token identity across EVM chains. It is included because an attacker abused the Holograph Operator contract in June 2024 to mint one billion unauthorized HLG tokens, prompting a protocol lock, exchange-account freezes, a burn plan, and an investigation involving Halborn and law enforcement.
brand_history_notes: In 2024 the domain described an omnichain tokenization protocol. At the 2026 review, the same domain described an onchain creator-coin trading terminal and no longer documented the historical cross-chain protocol. This record therefore treats the historical interoperability product as inactive without asserting a legally or technically continuous successor relationship.
notes: The one-billion-HLG unauthorized mint is not automatically treated as a one-billion-token realized loss. Minted, sold, frozen, and burned quantities remain distinct, and completion of the announced burn plan is unresolved.

summary: The Inter-Blockchain Communication Protocol (IBC) is an open-source, permissionless interoperability protocol for transferring tokens, messages, and arbitrary application data between sovereign blockchains. It is included because the Dragonberry and Huckleberry disclosures required coordinated security responses across IBC-connected infrastructure, while official accounts report no exploitation or user-fund loss from those vulnerabilities.
brand_history_notes: IBC Classic was first deployed in March 2021. ibc-go is the principal Go implementation and is modeled as implementation context under the protocol entity rather than as a separate bridge entity.
notes: Dragonberry and Huckleberry are modeled as security-response events rather than exploit incidents because official sources describe vulnerability discovery, coordinated patching, and no known loss.

terminal_reason: Ren 1.0 entered a planned sunset after Alameda-related funding ended; the reviewed current site still describes Ren 2.0 as coming soon.
brand_history_notes: RenVM was the MPC network and RenBridge was an application using it. They remain context under the Ren Protocol entity rather than separate canonical bridge entities.
notes: No incident record is created for the 2022 sunset. Ren 2.0 is not linked as a successor because reviewed evidence does not establish a public mainnet launch.
summary: Ren Protocol operated RenVM and RenBridge as cross-chain infrastructure for native assets including Bitcoin. The reviewed Ren 1.0 lineage ended after Alameda-related funding stopped in late 2022, while Ren 2.0 remained announced but not verified as a public mainnet successor.

terminal_reason: Officially replaced by Avalanche Bridge on July 29, 2021; AEB transfers were subsequently disabled and legacy assets moved to an upgrade path.
brand_history_notes: AEB used the earlier ChainBridge-style relayer architecture. The successor Avalanche Bridge is a separate canonical entity.
notes: Residual support for upgrading deprecated AEB assets is legacy support and does not make AEB active.
summary: The Avalanche-Ethereum Bridge was Avalanche's first official Ethereum bridge. It launched in February 2021 and was replaced in July 2021 by the SGX-based Avalanche Bridge, followed by relayer shutdown and migration of bridged assets.

operator_name: Ava Labs and Bridge Node operators
brand_history_notes: Launched as the next-generation replacement for AEB with a distinct SGX and Bridge Node architecture.
notes: Batch 5 establishes the predecessor relationship and current active status; it does not claim to provide a complete incident history for the current bridge.
summary: Avalanche Bridge is the SGX and Bridge Node based official bridge connecting Ethereum and Avalanche C-Chain. It launched on July 29, 2021 as the explicit replacement for the Avalanche-Ethereum Bridge and remains supported through Core.

terminal_reason: Bridge operations migrated to Zero Gravity in November 2023, followed by a claim-only period and final ShuttleFlow website and dApp shutdown in January 2024.
brand_history_notes: Official closure material described a technology and operational handoff to Zero Gravity. KinetFlow later replaced Zero Gravity Portal using technology from both services.
notes: No successor_id is set because Zero Gravity is not a reviewed canonical entity in this batch.
summary: ShuttleFlow was Conflux's cross-chain asset protocol and multi-chain bridge. Bridge operations ended in November 2023 with technology and service migration to Zero Gravity, while a limited claim path remained until the website and dApp closed in January 2024.

Transit Swap is a cross-chain swap and routing aggregator operated under Transit Finance. It is included because an October 2022 approval and routing-contract exploit exposed user assets, followed by substantial attacker returns, a service suspension, contract replacement, security hardening, and relaunch.
brand_history_notes: Transit Finance is the operator and broader product identity; Transit Swap is the canonical cross-chain swap product recorded by BIR.
notes: The October 2022 case is modeled as an aggregator routing and approval incident, not as a compromise of every integrated bridge or DEX.

summary: Magpie Protocol is a cross-chain liquidity and swap aggregator whose current public product identity is Fly. It is included because an April 2024 MagpieRouterV2 validation flaw exposed approved wallet assets, followed by a pause, contract remediation, full protocol-funded reimbursement, security work, and reopening.
brand_history_notes: Current first-party publishing and the live product use Fly while retaining Magpie naming in documentation, support, deployments, and community material. This record does not yet assert a separate successor entity.
notes: Wormhole was a messaging dependency; the reviewed incident affected MagpieRouterV2 and is not classified as a Wormhole compromise.

summary: Rubic is a cross-chain swap and bridge aggregator. It is included because a November 2022 private-key compromise affected the wallet used by its former RBC/BRBC bridge and a separate December 2022 RubicProxy flaw exposed approved user USDC, followed by contract suspension, replacement, audits, and continuing operation.
brand_history_notes: The former native RBC/BRBC bridge was disabled and replaced by external bridge infrastructure. That historical component is not treated as currently active merely because the Rubic aggregator remains active.
notes: The November and December 2022 cases have different targets, causes, loss scopes, and aftermath and remain separate incidents.

summary: Unizen is a trade and cross-chain aggregator whose Unizen Interoperability Protocol routes through third-party interoperability providers. It is included because a March 2024 external-call flaw exposed approved user assets, followed by a bounty and law-enforcement response, reimbursement commencement, partial recovery, contract changes, audits, and continuing operation.
notes: The March 2024 incident affected Unizen's trade-aggregation contract and approved user assets. Integrated UIP providers are not classified as compromised.

summary: Taiko Bridge is Taiko's first-party canonical bridge between Ethereum and Taiko. In June 2026, forged L2 proof/state data enabled fraudulent withdrawals from the canonical Bridge and ERC20Vault after an exposed SGX prover signing key and an attestation check that failed to reject debug-enabled enclaves undermined the prover trust boundary. Taiko paused the affected paths, restored the pre-attack state, recollateralized the bridge 1:1, made users whole, and reopened the bridge on July 2 under conservative quotas.
operator_name: Taiko Labs and Taiko protocol contributors
brand_history_notes: The canonical entity covers Taiko's official Ethereum-facing Bridge and ERC20Vault withdrawal path. The first-party postmortem says the ZK proving math and Bridge contracts themselves were not the exploited bug; forged finalized L2 state was accepted upstream and then consumed by the normal withdrawal path.
notes: Current active status follows the July 2 reopening. User backing and compensation are complete, while attacker-fund recovery remains partial and law-enforcement recovery remains open.

summary: Everclear, previously known as Connext, was a cross-chain interoperability and clearing protocol. It is included as a lifecycle record covering Connext bridge history, the Everclear rebrand and clearing-layer launch, and the 2026 shutdown of the protocol, UI, chain, Foundation, and Labs operations.
terminal_reason: The operator announced the wind-down after the protocol, UI, and chain had been sunset and commercial operations were not sustainable.
brand_history_notes: Connext evolved into Everclear in 2024. The rebrand and protocol evolution are represented within one canonical entity rather than predecessor and successor entities.
notes: This is a lifecycle-only record. Publicly accessible documentation after shutdown is retained as historical evidence and is not proof of active protocol operation.

summary: Commons Bridge was the official bridge for moving SYND among Ethereum, Base, and Commons Chain. It is included because an April 2026 bridge-proxy compromise was followed by automatic treasury-funded reimbursement, an additional 15 percent payment, and the permanent wind-down of Commons network and bridge operations.
terminal_reason: Commons network and its bridge were wound down after the bridge compromise and reimbursement process.
brand_history_notes: Commons Bridge is separated from the broader Syndicate Bridge family because the compromised Commons route and network were permanently wound down while other Syndicate route descriptions may remain available.
notes: The Syndicate Labs wind-down is related operator context, not the asserted cause of the bridge compromise.

summary: Syscoin UTXO–NEVM Bridge is Syscoin's native asset bridge between its UTXO and NEVM layers. It is included because a June 2026 cross-layer interpretation exploit released 5 billion unauthorized SYS; the full amount was later returned and burned, while the bridge remained paused in the latest explicit reviewed first-party status.
brand_history_notes: This record is the UTXO–NEVM bridge affected in June 2026. It is distinct from Syscoin's separate trustless Bitcoin bridge work and UTXO-to-Rollux bridge development.
notes: The June 2026 unauthorized 5 billion SYS release was fully returned and burned, restoring the reported coin supply. Financial recovery is complete, but bridge operations remained paused in the latest explicit reviewed first-party status.

summary: TAC Inner Bridge is TAC's native lock-and-mint cross-chain framework connecting TON and TAC. It is included because its sequencer message-validation path was exploited in May 2026, causing unbacked minting on TAC and release of real locked assets on TON. TAC reported partial attacker-fund recovery and a Foundation backstop for the remaining shortfall, while the latest explicit reviewed first-party bridge state remained paused pending patched sequencer review and staged redeployment.
brand_history_notes: This record covers TAC's first-party TON ↔ TAC Inner Bridge / cross-chain framework. Third-party TAC routes such as Stargate, Hyperlane, or LayerZero are not included in the incident boundary merely because the attacker later used external cross-chain infrastructure.
notes: The May 2026 incident had approximately $2.854 million protocol loss and $2.291 million final net recovery. TAC announced a treasury backstop for the remaining shortfall, but reviewed first-party evidence did not establish completed reimbursement/liquidity restoration or bridge reopening.

summary: XRPL-TX Bridge is the current TX-era identity of the bridge historically documented as XRPL-Coreum Bridge. It connects XRP Ledger and TX through an XRPL multi-signing account, a TX-side bridge contract, and a relayer set. Independent on-chain reporting says approximately 200,000 XRP left the bridge on August 9, 2026; the bridge was reported halted while the incident remained unresolved.
brand_history_notes: Current TX documentation names the system XRPL-TX Bridge; historical Coreum documentation names the same relayer / multisig / bridge-contract architecture XRPL-Coreum Bridge. BIR models this as one lifecycle entity unless later first-party material establishes a technically separate redeployment.
notes: The August 2026 incident is public with medium confidence while root cause, recovery, reimbursement, and final restart outcome remain under review. The presence of a relayer signature quorum is not treated as proof of relayer-key compromise.

summary: WanBridge is Wanchain's decentralized non-custodial cross-chain value-transfer bridge. A Cardano–BNB Chain route carrying NIGHT suffered a major July 2026 incident in which roughly 515 million NIGHT were reported drained from the Cardano side. The broader WanBridge product remains documented and publicly available, but that does not establish that the affected NIGHT route itself reopened.
brand_history_notes: Wanchain documentation brands the direct value-transfer product as WanBridge, while incident reporting refers to Wanchain Bridge. BIR treats those names as one bridge entity unless later first-party material establishes a separate route-specific product identity.
notes: Entity status reflects the broader WanBridge service, not proof that the affected Cardano–BNB NIGHT route reopened. Route-specific restart remains unresolved in the incident record.

summary: ChainConnect is a multi-chain EVM↔TVM asset bridge. A July 2026 incident exploited missing sender verification in an Alien Proxy callback, enabling unbacked Alien TIP-3 minting and transfer through the bridge flow to Ethereum. ChainConnect paused bridge operations and patched affected deployments; a dated post-incident reopening has not been established in the reviewed first-party record.
brand_history_notes: BIR treats ChainConnect as the bridge product identified by its official application, documentation, and announcement channel. Reachability of the application after the incident is not treated as proof that incident-affected bridge routes reopened.
notes: The latest explicit reviewed incident-era operational statement records a bridge pause. A later patch and partial attacker-fund return do not by themselves establish bridge reopening or user reimbursement.

summary: Verus-Ethereum Bridge is Verus's non-custodial bridge between Verus and Ethereum. A second 2026 exploit on July 23 used the Ethereum import path to trigger unbacked payouts from bridge reserves. Verus later referenced the latest Ethereum bridge hack in its v1.2.17-3 security release while stating that Ethereum contracts were not yet ready for upgrade; a dated post-incident reopening has not been established.
notes: This bridge has separate May and July 2026 canonical incidents. May attacker-fund recovery, restitution and reopen evidence is scoped only to the May incident; July recovery, reimbursement and post-incident reopening remain unresolved. Current bridge status remains paused after the later July incident.

summary: Axelar–Secret IBC Bridge is the asset-transfer connection used by Secret Tunnel for Axelar-wrapped assets on Secret Network. In June 2026, the Secret-side ics20-for-axelar contract accepted inbound token messages without authenticating the legitimate source channel, enabling unbacked wrapped-asset minting and redemption against real Axelar-side reserves. The affected connection was disabled and remains non-operational at the latest review.
brand_history_notes: BIR scopes this record to the Axelar–Secret asset-transfer connection and Secret-side ics20-for-axelar contract. The June 2026 incident did not establish compromise of Axelar core, IBC generally, Secret Network consensus/privacy, or unrelated Secret IBC connections.
notes: Current paused status is supported by Secret Tunnel's continuing non-operational incident notice. Axelar governance Proposal #490 is a non-binding recovery/distribution signal and is not evidence of completed recovery or reimbursement.

summary: AFX Bridge is the AFX-operated custody bridge associated with AFX Trade's Arbitrum-based trading infrastructure. On July 22, 2026, a software-supply-chain and internal-infrastructure compromise reached a subset of AFX validator nodes, which then co-signed a bridge-contract transfer of 24,150,000 USDC. AFX suspended bridge operations and froze the bridge contract; a dated post-incident reopening has not been established.
brand_history_notes: BIR uses AFXTrade's verified first-party Medium publication channel as the public operator locator. The incident is scoped to AFX-operated custody-bridge and validator infrastructure and not to Arbitrum or Arbitrum's native bridge.
notes: Latest explicit first-party incident-era state is suspended/frozen. Infrastructure rebuilding and hardening are not treated as bridge-reopen evidence.

summary: Oraichain-operated EVM cross-chain transfer path affected by an August 2026 unauthorized ORAI minting incident. Oraichain later restored the network and completed on-chain restoration, but the reviewed first-party material does not separately prove full post-incident restoration of the affected cross-chain path.
brand_history_notes: This is a conservative descriptive BIR entity name derived from incident-specific first-party wording. It is not a claim that the affected production path was branded OBridge or OraiBridge.
notes: Network return-to-service is established, but full affected cross-chain-path reopening is not separately established; entity status remains limited.

summary: QANplatform operated a QANX bridge between Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain. The bridge wallet was hacked on 2022-10-11, after which QANplatform replaced the affected QANX token contract and opened a recovery and compensation process.
notes: Current bridge operating status is kept unknown; the reviewed sources establish the 2022 bridge-wallet hack and token replacement/compensation process, not a later bridge restart.

summary: BXH operated cross-chain bridge functionality within its DeFi platform. BXH states that a September 21, 2022 security incident affected user assets including cross-chain bridge positions, followed by a compensation program and an announced exit from the DeFi product.
terminal_reason: BXH announced that its DeFi platform would exit and compensation work would move toward the BXH Exchange.
notes: HECO and OEC are named in the first-party compensation material but are retained as unknown chain references here because BIR does not currently define dedicated HECO/OEC reference keys. Bridge-only USD loss is intentionally not inferred from mixed LP/bridge material.

summary: Cellframe operates a bridge for assets including USDC. In a May 2026 AMA, the team said it had announced a bridge hack and illegal token issuance, then hardened the bridge by separating hot and cold components and moving USDC away from older protocols while investigation continued.
notes: Current operation is kept limited because the official May 2026 AMA describes ongoing investigation and hardening but does not establish a fully resolved incident boundary or total damage.

summary: deBridge is a cross-chain interoperability protocol for transferring assets, messages, and transaction data across supported blockchains. Its first-party history places mainnet launch on February 17, 2022, initially supporting Ethereum, BNB Chain, HECO, Arbitrum, and Polygon.
notes: HECO is represented by the existing unknown chain reference because BIR has no dedicated HECO reference key. The reviewed 2022 attempted cyberattack is not canonicalized as an incident in this batch.

summary: Gnosis OmniBridge is the native token bridge connecting Ethereum and Gnosis Chain. Gnosis documentation states that OmniBridge is built on top of the Arbitrary Message Bridge (AMB), shares its validator trust model, and mints canonical representations of bridged assets on Gnosis.
brand_history_notes: Current Gnosis documentation distinguishes the current bridge UI from the legacy OmniBridge interface.
notes: Gnosis Chain is represented by the existing unknown chain reference because BIR has no dedicated Gnosis Chain reference key. Legacy/current UI changes and historical pauses are not treated as exploit incidents.

summary: Hop Protocol is a token bridge designed to move assets across Ethereum scaling networks and their shared layer-1. Hop announced mainnet availability in July 2021, initially live on Ethereum, Polygon, and xDai before expanding to additional rollups.
brand_history_notes: This record describes the reviewed Hop bridge lifecycle. v2 development is not used to infer deprecation or death of v1.
notes: xDai/Gnosis is represented by the existing unknown chain reference because BIR has no dedicated Gnosis Chain reference key. No incident is added in this batch.

summary: Across began as a cross-chain token bridge and now describes itself as a crosschain interoperability protocol using an intents-based architecture. Across launched on mainnet in November 2021 and its current unified API powers crosschain swaps, bridges, and embedded actions.
brand_history_notes: Across evolved from its original L2 bridge design into an intents-based interoperability protocol; this is treated as one continuing canonical entity.
notes: Absence of a reviewed major hack is not a safety claim and no incident is inferred in this batch.

summary: Stargate is a cross-chain asset-transfer and global-liquidity protocol. Stargate documentation identifies V1 as the foundational native-asset transfer mechanism introduced in March 2022, using unified liquidity and LayerZero messaging; current materials describe Stargate as a global liquidity layer.
brand_history_notes: V1 and V2 are retained as lifecycle/architecture context inside one Stargate canonical entity rather than split into separate bridge entities.
notes: Current multi-chain breadth is not flattened into an exhaustive chain list here. No exploit incident is inferred in this batch.

summary: Meson is a cross-chain asset-transfer and swap protocol. First-party material announced its mainnet launch on December 1, 2021 with initial stablecoin routes across BNB Chain, Polygon, Fantom, and Avalanche.
notes: The record captures Meson as a bridge/cross-chain transfer protocol. Marketing security claims are not treated as safety findings, and no incident is inferred in this batch.

summary: Symbiosis is a cross-chain liquidity and token-routing protocol supporting bridging, cross-chain swaps, and interchain operations. First-party material launched the V1 beta mainnet on March 9, 2022; current documentation describes V2 as the successor retaining the core cross-chain model.
brand_history_notes: Symbiosis V1 later reached end of life and V2 became its direct successor. No exact V1 shutdown date is inferred here.
notes: Current documentation describes bridging as one of several cross-chain operations. No exploit, loss, recovery, or reimbursement record is inferred in this batch.

summary: Orbiter Finance is a decentralized cross-rollup bridge and interoperability protocol. First-party material from December 2021 states that Orbiter Alpha had launched with transfers among Ethereum mainnet, zkSync, and Arbitrum.
brand_history_notes: Later first-party material describes an evolution from bridge toward broader rollup/interoperability infrastructure; this record keeps the bridge lineage within one canonical entity.
notes: zkSync is represented by the existing unknown chain reference because BIR has no dedicated zkSync reference key. The source proves Alpha was live by 2021-12-30, not that December 30 was the exact launch date.

summary: Router Protocol is a cross-chain bridge and interoperability protocol. First-party material announced its public alpha mainnet on January 27, 2022, supporting cross-chain transfers, swaps, and arbitrary messaging.
brand_history_notes: Router later expanded toward Nitro, Router Chain, and chain-abstraction/interoperability infrastructure. Those developments are retained as lifecycle context inside the same protocol identity.
notes: No incident or security outcome is inferred from protocol architecture or later product evolution.

summary: ChainPort is a cross-chain asset bridge. First-party material shows it operating as a permissionless blockchain bridge in 2021, and later first-party history explicitly states that ChainPort launched in 2021.
brand_history_notes: Current ChainPort supports several bridging architectures within one product lineage.
notes: Security and custody claims in first-party materials are treated only as source context, not as BIR safety ratings. No incident is inferred in this batch.

summary: Mayan is cross-chain swap and execution infrastructure built around Wormhole-connected routing and later intent-based transfer methods. First-party material shows Mayan operating as cross-chain swap infrastructure in 2022; the exact initial launch day is not established here.
brand_history_notes: Wormhole Swap, Swift/MCTP, and Mayan 2.0 are retained as architecture/lifecycle evolution within one Mayan canonical entity.
notes: An official October 26, 2022 post already describes Mayan as cross-chain swap infrastructure connected to five networks. The record therefore uses conservative 2022 year precision rather than the looser later phrase 'since our launch one year ago'. No incident is inferred.

summary: rhino.fi is a multichain DeFi platform with cross-chain swaps and a collateralized bridge model. First-party material marks July 13, 2022 as the rhino.fi rebrand and launch of cross-chain swaps with Polygon.

summary: Butter Bridge V3.1 provided the MAPO cross-chain service between legacy ERC-20 MAPO and MAP Protocol mainnet MAPO. On May 20, 2026, the OmniServiceProxy path was exploited to mint unauthorized MAPO on Ethereum and BNB Chain. MAP Protocol states that mainnet consensus, native MAPO, light-client verification, Oracle multisig, and project-team keys were unaffected; the affected service was suspended and remediation followed.
brand_history_notes: This record is scoped to the affected Butter Bridge V3.1 cross-chain service and does not represent MAP Protocol mainnet as compromised.
notes: MAPO has no dedicated BIR asset-reference key and MAP Protocol has no dedicated chain key, so those references remain unknown. A later audited-contract deployment and compensation framework are recorded without inferring completed reimbursement or unrestricted bridge reopening.

summary: Garden Finance is a cross-chain atomic-swap protocol using HTLCs and independent solvers. Two separate solver-layer security incidents are recorded: an October 2025 compromise of a solver operating environment and a July 2026 compromise of an independent solver’s off-chain database. Garden states that protocol contracts and user funds were not compromised in either incident.
notes: Both incidents are scoped to solver infrastructure. Solver-owned losses are not converted into user-loss or protocol-contract-compromise claims. Latest unrestricted service restoration after the July 2026 pause is not established in the admitted incident evidence.
